subject.title: [Feature]: LLM distillation/extraction gate for memory-core deep-phase promotion (distill, don't dump raw snippets into MEMORY.md)

question: Should `memory-core` add a narrow opt-in LLM distillation gate for dreaming promotion now, or should this remain folded into the broader lifecycle-aware memory curator tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87660?
rationale: The code can filter known raw artifacts today, but model-backed rewriting before durable memory writes changes product semantics, config surface, fallback behavior, and long-term memory ownership.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle curator
options.body: Keep this issue open as overlapping product input and implement distillation together with the broader durable/stale/locked memory lifecycle design.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in distillation
options.body: Define a small disabled-by-default extraction contract, reviewable output schema, fallback behavior, and tests for both distilled and non-distilled promotion paths.

options.title: Keep deterministic filtering only
options.body: Decline LLM rewriting for now and continue improving the existing raw-contamination and threshold gates without adding model-backed memory mutation.

recommendation.title: Fold into lifecycle curator
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as overlapping product input and implement distillation together with the broader durable/stale/locked memory lifecycle design.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current dreaming promotion flow and thresholds, making them the best history-backed routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
